Version changelog

v0.119.1 · Bugfix · Reserve galaxy 1:1 for staff 2026-10-14
  • New Player accounts begin outside galaxy1:1; staff accounts retain access to its registration slots.
  • The existing Multihunter planet at1:1:2 remains in place after checking its account role. No planet is moved or reset.
  • Existing planetary assets and alliance membership are preserved.
Full news article →
v0.119.0 · Alliance planning and staff control 2026-10-14
  • One-minute caches reduce repeated public asset decoding and public data requests. Private profiles, permissions and gameplay writes retain fresh authorisation.
  • Support and Multihunter permission nodes are configurable on Account ranks. Saves are audited and revision-checked; only Administrators can edit the matrix or grant Administrator rank.
  • Network Hub fleet panels and intel controls have consistent spacing across themes, with wrapped controls and scrollable tables.
  • The alliance attack tool now adapts pa-tools operations, scheduled openings, prereleases, consecutive wave bookings and shared ownership. Existing claims are imported; revisions prevent conflicting claims. The full Battlegroup page remains queued under SF-032.
  • General forum is available inside the game alongside the private galaxy and alliance forums. Private membership checks remain in place.
Full news article →
v0.117.2 · Bugfix · Research bonuses finish the active project 2026-10-14
  • Bonus RP now clears the active research slot when that level completes, including levels below the branch maximum.
  • Surplus allocated RP remains attached to the next level; unspent bonus points remain in the bonus bank.
  • The current round is preserved.
Full news article →
v0.117.1 · Bugfix · Empty founding fleets and restored ministerial navigation 2026-10-14
  • Founding ships, the base fleet and all four fleets start empty. Ships must be built or granted through an explicit game action.
  • The Government ministerial-register button uses the game navigation handler.
  • The requested reset renews the round and registration drafts while preserving accounts and stored diagnostic reports.
Full news article →
v0.116.2 · Bugfix · Accurate diagnostics and progress feedback 2026-10-14
  • Current-page errors and historical errors are stored separately. Reloading no longer adds another timestamp to old errors.
  • Diagnostic samples report new errors from that page load. Closed disclosures, hidden controls and transparent elements no longer produce false viewport warnings.
  • Layout warnings identify the visible controls involved. Reports record the deployed version.
  • A progress bar advances after each completed browser page check and after the report is saved, with the current stage and completed count.
  • The current round is preserved.
Full news article →
v0.116.1 · Bugfix · Editable planet names 2026-10-14
  • The registration name field is editable for every world. A reference name is used as its initial suggestion.
  • The server keeps the entered player name instead of forcing the reference name. Planet Settings can rename an existing reference-world colony.
  • World type, artwork, unique reservation and special bonuses remain attached to the same world; naming cannot create a second copy.
  • The current round is preserved.
Full news article →
v0.116.0 · Staff diagnostics and ancestral world charters 2026-10-14
  • Staff can run system diagnostics, inspect saved reports and export JSON. Checks cover internal links, anchors, missing assets, metadata and sampled browser runtime/layout observations.
  • All staff ranks may inspect reports without owning a planet; players cannot open the page or its API. Reports survive round resets.
  • Frontier Worlds now includes twenty active original environments. Five once-per-round Ancestral Thrones apply their racial theme and grant 10% ship resource discounts, multiplied with government discounts.
  • Catalogue families use generic names, and paged requests retrieve only the visible surveys. Assignment changes that alter a theme reload the game once.
  • Scan sharing retries a failed initial connection and offers a visible retry control. Confirmed server settings remain authoritative.
  • The user-requested reset removes active planets, renews registration and rerolls, releases world reservations and stops the ticker. Accounts, Owner recovery keys and diagnostic reports remain.
  • A general visual polish pass and expanded family artwork await explicit user authorisation after the reset.
Full news article →
v0.115.2 · Bugfix · Reliable game startup and restored modules 2026-10-14
  • The game loads one ordered runtime instead of seventeen separate scripts; failed downloads retry automatically without applying a partial startup.
  • Rendering starts after the complete runtime is initialised. The connection panel provides a retry button when downloads remain unavailable.
  • The browser receives a versioned runtime URL. Error logs identify failed files and JavaScript source locations.
  • The game loads a small world seed and receives the actual planet surveys with its directory, rather than parsing the complete reference catalogue on every visit.
  • Background polls pause when the page is hidden. This bugfix preserves the current round and does not perform another reset.
Full news article →
v0.115.1 · Bugfix · Faster loading and staff access corrections 2026-10-14
  • Portal typography uses immediate theme-matched fallback fonts; external blocking font imports are removed. Large videos load only when played, with preload disabled.
  • Access auditing runs after the response through the Worker execution context. Schema and authenticated-request lookups are reused, and binary assets decode without per-byte array callbacks.
  • Players’ manual removes staff-only chapters, controls and editorial modules. Staff manual is served only after authentication and staff-role checks.
  • Administrator, Support and Multihunter manuals expose procedures relevant to that role, with a common permissions matrix and evidence-handling guide.
  • Spacing Bank policy and Site management remain Administrator responsibilities. Support has tickets and read-only staff audit; Multihunters has access, fleet investigation and read-only audit.
  • Staff tools continue to work without a personal planet. This documentation update does not reset the round again.
Full news article →
v0.115.0 · World charters, expanded quest offices and the Spacing Bank Collective 2026-10-14
  • Final charter confirmation uses two columns: identity and controls on the left, planet artwork and full stats on the right.
  • The mobile confirmation stacks both panels and remains scrollable. Planet assignment and entered values stay unchanged.
  • Round-reset wording now reflects removal of planets followed by new charter registration.
  • Planet Overview displays the same assigned-world artwork as colonial registration, with type, habitability, growth modifier and starting housing.
  • Planet register: named Star Trek and Dune worlds, twenty once-per-round Borg/Undine worlds, Earth, Ultimate Arrakis and Unimatrix999 Homeworld. Lore-inspired ecology and generated gameplay survey values are labelled.
  • Registration stays fixed across refresh and permits three server-counted rerolls. Unique names and reservations prevent duplicate world charters. Ordinary worlds at 60% habitability or lower leave new selection; special worlds are exempt.
  • Arrakis has −1 tick fleet travel for the round; Earth receives 20% bonus salvage from destroyed attackers and defenders when it participates. Unique charter broadcasts conceal the holder and coordinates.
  • Exclusive Silver, Borg, Undine, Legendary, Ultimate and Unimatrix999 styles apply automatically and appear only for the corresponding holder and staff.
  • Every achievement office offers at least fifteen supported goals, in an ordered upper menu. The summary tab contains statistics. New rewards include resources, CU, RP, settlers and research-gated structures; blocked structures convert to their CU cost.
  • Spaceport adds the finite Spacing Bank Collective, starting at one million of each resource per round. Staff controls tax, values and limits; admins configure next-round starting reserves. Exchange receipts settle atomically.
  • Five-character read-only account IDs appear on profiles and command cards. Staff workspaces operate without a planet, and round settings display an inline saved timestamp.
  • Staff overview and the new portal Staff page show a full personnel roster and duties. Staff and the placeholder Round history page are linked in the top menu.
  • Galaxy Browser initially opens the player’s own galaxy and includes a Go to 1:1 button. Leading Of is omitted in the planetary command display.
  • Site management retains the news editor and adds global toggles for Round history demo examples and the simulated battle lab. Real completed round archives automatically replace fictional examples.
